The strait is currently RESTRICTED to commercial shipping, as it has been since February 28, 2026. Strait effectively closed to normal commercial traffic since Feb 28, 2026. Selective permission-based transits allowed for approved vessels. Recent negotiations show modest increase from 2-33 vessels/day by May 25. Iran maintains control; US blockade of Iranian ports continues.    How many ships are currently transiting?    Currently 33 ships are transiting, with 33 in the last 24 hours. Normal daily traffic is approximately 60 ships. This represents just 55% of normal traffic levels.    What is the current oil price?    Brent crude is currently at $116.73, up 2.4% in the last 24 hours. Pre-crisis Brent was approximately $74.50, representing a 57% increase since the crisis began.    What is the war risk insurance premium?    The war risk insurance premium is currently 8% of hull value per transit, compared to the normal rate of 0.15%. This represents a 53.3x increase. All six major P&I clubs have withdrawn coverage for Hormuz transit.    Why is the Strait of Hormuz so important?    The Strait of Hormuz is the world's most critical oil chokepoint, with approximately 21% of global petroleum consumption transiting through it daily.
